messages.content:
You are a clinical validator checking whether a PTSD case
vignette accurately reflects a patient's required cognitive connections.

You will receive:
- A vignette to validate
- A list of REQUIRED edges that must appear
- A list of ACTIVE components that must appear

---

COMPONENT SYNONYMS
Each component may appear by its exact name or any accepted synonym:
  Triggers            → "triggers", "reminders", "cues", "triggering stimuli"
  Negative Appraisals → "negative appraisals", "negative beliefs", "appraisals", "distorted beliefs"
  Memory              → "intrusive memory", "trauma memory", "traumatic memory", "the memory"
  Threat              → "sense of threat", "perceived threat", "threat", "feeling of danger"
  Maladaptive Strategies → "maladaptive strategies", "avoidance", "maladaptive coping", "safety behaviours"

---

CAUSAL STANDARD
A required edge A→B is SATISFIED if, within the same paragraph:
  - Both A and B (or their synonyms) appear, AND
  - The paragraph conveys — through any language — that A influences, drives, or leads to B.
This includes direct causal sentences, sequential structure, or connecting phrases
like "because of", "this meant", "so", "which led", "as a result", "consequently", "in turn".
A required edge is MISSING only if no paragraph conveys the A→B relationship at all.

---

SECTION 1 — COMPONENT CHECK
Active components (must appear in the vignette):
  - Maladaptive Strategies
  - Memory
  - Negative Appraisals
  - Threat
  - Triggers

Confirm each component appears as a described feature of the patient's presentation.
This is an internal check only — do NOT add component results to violations.

---

SECTION 2 — REQUIRED EDGES
  - Triggers → Maladaptive Strategies
  - Triggers → Threat
  - Triggers → Memory
  - Triggers → Negative Appraisals
  - Negative Appraisals → Maladaptive Strategies
  - Negative Appraisals → Threat
  - Negative Appraisals → Memory
  - Memory → Threat
  - Memory → Negative Appraisals
  - Memory → Triggers
  - Threat → Maladaptive Strategies
  - Threat → Memory
  - Threat → Negative Appraisals
  - Threat → Triggers
  - Maladaptive Strategies → Negative Appraisals
  - Maladaptive Strategies → Triggers

For each edge, apply the causal standard above.
- If satisfied: do nothing — only failures are reported.
- If missing: add it to violations and explain in one sentence what causal relationship is absent.

Validate the following vignette against the cognitive graph.

Darius was twenty-four when the downtown zoning protest fractured into chaos. He had been positioned near a makeshift press line, notebook in hand, when the first line of riot police surged forward without warning. The heavy tread of boots closing in from his blind spot, paired with a distorted R&B track bleeding from a nearby storefront radio, instantly anchored him to the brick wall pressing against his back. The violence was not a cinematic sequence but a suffocating proximity to force that left his nervous system permanently keyed to the sounds of pursuit. In the weeks that followed, those specific sensory cues ceased to be mere background noise; they became immediate catalysts for a hyper-vivid reconstruction of the raid. His memories of the event felt more real and tangible than his present reality, complete with sharp auditory recall of the radio static and shouted commands echoing in his skull. This relentless sensory intrusion made it impossible for him to speak about the night without losing his thread, leaving him stranded in the middle of a story he could no longer finish. Yet it was the lingering echo of the past that constantly pulled him back into states of acute trigger sensitivity, as every faint footfall or familiar chord reactivated the visceral panic of that night. Because the memories felt so viscerally present, Darius became convinced that the danger had never actually receded. He began scanning every environment, frequently checking behind him to verify no one was trailing him, and refusing to enter unfamiliar neighborhoods where he could not assess the danger. During his morning editorial meetings, the clack of keyboard keys and the distant hum of the city transit system would suddenly morph into the cadence of advancing boots and sirens. Each accidental auditory overlap would immediately pull his attention away from his current assignments, leaving him staring at a blank screen while his pulse spiked. His hypervigilance actively drained his ability to focus, forcing him to draft articles in isolated corners and miss deadlines that required collaboration. The constant cognitive load of threat monitoring also kept his nervous system locked in a state of high alert, which paradoxically prevented his traumatic memories from integrating, leaving them fresh and unprocessed. As his concentration deteriorated, he found himself increasingly unable to perform the investigative reporting that had once defined him, which quickly solidified his conviction that his life had been destroyed by the trauma. Believing he was fundamentally broken, he adopted a strategy of emotional flattening and physical concealment, wearing high-collared coats to stay unseen and deliberately steering clear of veteran parades or joyful family gatherings that might stir emotion. This deliberate avoidance of grief reminders and all feelings only deepened his negative self-appraisals, reinforcing his belief that he had permanently lost his happiness and was no longer capable of living as he once did. Yet his concealment and emotional numbing kept him isolated in familiar, safe zones, where the very lack of novelty made ordinary background sounds feel disproportionately potent and trigger another wave of panic. His narrowed world, in turn, fed his threat appraisal that the environment was inherently hostile, which further paralyzed his ability to work and pushed him deeper into the clinic. Now, at twenty-five, the weight of this closed loop finally forced him into therapy because his girlfriend had noticed he was disappearing into his own head during meals, and he was terrified that his professional credibility was collapsing alongside his personal life. He hoped for a way to silence the echoing radio static and walk through a crowded street without checking his six, though he feared that facing the past would only confirm that he was utterly ruined.
